full_judgment:
2. The facts, relevant for disposal of this petition, are that the petitioner and others as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.58 of 2012 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Bancharampur, Brahmanbaria for permanent injunction stating, inter alia, that one Gazi Mamud sold out 15 decimals land out of 31 decimals land of CS Plot No.846 to one Kamar Uddin, father of Abdul Awal before 40 years. After two years, said Abdul Awal sold out that land to one Yusuf Ali and others and handed over the possession, but no registered deed was executed between them. Subsequently, afore-said Gazi Marnud, Abdul Awal, Dhanu Miah, Yusuf Ali and Momen Miah died leaving behind their respective heirs. The plaintiffs as heirs of Yusuf Ali are in possession in the suit land. The defendants had no title and possession over the suit land. Subsequently, the plaintiffs purchased the suit land from the heirs of Gazi Mamud vide three separate registered deeds being No.2304, 2305, 2306 dated 03.04.2012 respectively. On 20.04.2012, Defendant Nos.3-7 threatened to dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit land; hence the suit. 

 3. Defendant Nos.1-2 and 4 contested the suit by 'filing a written statement denying all allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the suit land originally belonged to Gazi Mamud, who sold out 15 decimals land out of 31 decimals land to Abdul Awal, father of defendant Nos.1 and 2 and grandfather of defendant No.4 vide registered deed No.1431 dated 12.02.1969. Thereafter, Abdul Awal died leaving behind his heirs defendant Nos.1 and 2 and one daughter, Sufia Khatun who got the possession of the suit land by way of amicable partition. Subsequently, defendant Nos.1 and 2 extended their homestead by way of cutting earth from the suit land. The plaintiffs have no right, title and possession over the suit land as such, the instant suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. The learned trial Court framed three issues for disposal of the suit. The plaintiffs side adduced 6(six) witnesses as PWs and the defendants side adduced 3(three) witnesses as DWs. 

 7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 05.10.2016 passed by the learned District Judge, Brahmanbaria, the defendants as petitioners moved before the High Court Division and the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division made the Rule absolute. Hence, plaintiffs as present-petitioners filed this civil petition for leave to appeal. 

 9. Mr. SK. Md. Morshed, learned Advocate, appearing for respondent Nos.1-2 and 6 supported the impugned judgment and decree of the High Court Division, but none appeared for other respondents. He further submits that the petitioner plaintiff has got no prima facie and arguable case to obtain an order of permanent injunction and as such the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division is very much justified in making the rule absolute. 

 12. The plaintiffs have come with an allegation that one Abdul Awal purchased the land from Gazi Mahamud and thereafter their predecessor Yusuf Ali, Dhanu Miah and Momin Miah purchased such land from Abdul Awal but there is no registered kabala for such purchase. It has been also claimed that the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land exclusively since their acquisition and as such, they prayed for an order of permanent injunction restraining the defendant so that they can-not disturb their exclusive possession. 

 13. On the other hand, contesting-defendant Nos.1, 2 and 4 denied the aforesaid contention of the plaintiffs and counter claim that Gazi Mahamud sold out .15 acre land to Abdul Awal who died leaving behind two sons, defendant Nos.1 and 2 and one daughter named Sufia Khatoon and aforesaid heirs of Abdul Awal have been possessing the suit land since acquisition and extended their homestead by way of cutting earth from the suit land. It has been further alleged that their predecessor, Abdul Awal never sold the suit land to the predecessor of the plaintiffs and there is no registered instrument of such transfer and as such, the plaintiffs have no right, title, interest and possession over the suit land as alleged and thus the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 14. The crux of the case is whether there was any fransfer by Abdul Awal in favour of the predecessor of the plaintiffs. In this respect, plaintiff Shafiqul Islam while deposing as PW1 clearly stated that there is no registered deed of transfer by Abdul Awal in favour of their predecessor and that it was an oral transfer. In course of cross examination, he stated that at the time of such transfer, he was a student of class seven. He further deposed that Gazi Mahmud transferred the suit land in the year 1969. He further deposed that he is now 54 years old. Thus, it stands that he was born in the year 1959 and on calculation, it appears that he was a boy of 10 years at the time of such oral transfer. It also appears to us that a boy of 10 years cannot be a student of class seven. Hence, there are intrinsic weaknesses and inherent infirmity in his evidence. Excepting PW1, the plaintiff-petitioner adduced no other witness with a view to prove the alleged fact of oral transfer. Over and above, as per provision of section 54 of Transfer of Property Act, an oral transfer cannot be a valid mode of transfer of land. It is not the case of the plaintiffs that the alleged transfer was not effected by registered instrument because the valuation of the suit land is less than 100/- taka. In this respect the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-respondent has cited a decision in the case of Gulshan-Vs- Ameer Ali reported in PLD 1997 (Kar) page 292 wherein it has been held that: "Mere agreement to sell would not confer any right, title or ownership inasmuch as any transaction of sale in respect of immovable property worth Taka 100 or upward was required to be compulsorily registered-Suit on basis of title, therefore, was not maintainable." 

 15. The plaintiffs further have come with an allegation that they have purchased the suit land from the heirs of Gazi Mahamud by dint of three kabalas. But it is admitted by the plaintiffs that Gazi Mahamud sold the suit land to one Kamar Uddin 40 years back who died leaving behind only son in Abdul Awal. It is admitted by both the parties that Gazi Mahamud sold the suit land to the predecessor of the defendants. Thus, we find that the heirs of Gazi Mahamud or his heirs had no saleable interest at the time of creation of three kabalas in favour of the plaintiffs. Thus, those three kabalas appear to be paper transaction which created no title in favour of the plaintiffs. Having considered the facts and circumstances and evidence on record, we find that the plaintiff-petitioner has no prima facie title and arguable case with a view to obtain an order of perpetual injunction. 

 16. This is a suit for permanent injunction. In such suit, the Court may enquire incidentally into the respective claims of the fact for determining whether the plaintiff is in possession of the suit property and entitled to the specific relief of permanent injunction. It is now well established by the consistent decisions of our apex Court that a suit for permanent injunction is maintainable where the plaintiff has been able to prove his exclusive possession in the suit property even though he may not have prima-facie title thereto. 

 17. Let us proceed to examine the evidence of record and see therefrom as to how far the petitioner-plaintiff has been able to prove the exclusive possession of the plaintiffs in the suit property. 

 18. PW1 Shafiqul Islam deposed that the predecessor of the plaintiffs got possession of the suit land in the year 1975. But he cannot say as to what was the actual date and month of getting such possession. He also admits that their predecessor never paid any rent for such land. PW2 deposed that he never went to the suit land. PW3 Abdul Mazid deposed that he is a man of 65 (sixty-five) years and he saw the predecessor of the plaintiffs to grow tobacco in the suit land at his age of 10/12 years. On calculation of his age, it appears to us that PW3 was born in the year 1948 and he saw the predecessor of the plain-tiffs to grow tobacco from the year 1958/1960. Whereas PW I deposed that their predecessor was inducted into possession of the suit land in the year 1975. PW4 Dhanesh Miah deposed that he knew the suit land but he never saw anybody to grow tobacco in the same. PW5 Sudhan Miah has contradicted with plaint in respect of naming the boundary men as has been described in the plaint. Thus, we find that the testimonies of the PWs are impeachable and full of contradictions. The facts and circumstances and evidence on record lead us to hold that the plaintiffs hopelessly failed to prove their exclusive possession over the suit land. Thus, the learned Judge of the High Court Division rightly appreciated the evidence on record and thereby set aside the concurrent findings of facts since there is apparent non- consideration and mis-appreciation of the evidence on record. 

 20. It is well settled that a plaintiff even though has no prima facie title may maintain a suit for permanent injunction if he can prove his exclusive possession over the suit property. In the instant case, the main question before us is whether the plaintiff-petitioner has succeeded in proving the plaintiffs' exclusive possession over the suit land. It appears that the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division has entered into the factual aspect of the case regarding possession and after thorough consideration of the same, came to the finding that the plaintiffs have not succeeded in proving their exclusive possession and disagreed with the finding of the Courts below. We have already seen that in a simple suit for permanent injunction with regard to a disputed landed property, the relief is available to a person who is in possession. 

 "The suit for permanent injunction is essentially a suit for possession. Though the title may be incidentally gone into but in a suit for permanent injunction the Court need not enter into disputed question of title except the extent, as it would help in finding which of the parties has possession. Plaintiff has failed to bring home their possession in the suit land for a decree for a permanent injunction." 

 22. From the facts and circumstances and the evidence on record, it appears that the plaintiff-petitioner was neither able to prove prima facie title nor the plaintiffs' possession.
